response.consequence: In mode 3 the legacy store stops receiving writes reliably. Legacy and unified storage diverge, and any rollback to an earlier mode loses data. The errors only show up as legacy failure metrics. The fix is to derive the goroutine context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx).
response.explanation: In Create (line 51), Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the legacy write runs in a goroutine. Its context comes from context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...), where ctx is the incoming request context. The handler returns right after launching the goroutine, and the API server then cancels the request context. The derived context is cancelled with it, so the 10s timeout never matters. The legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection calls usually run with an already-cancelled context and fail with context canceled, or are never performed. The old code made these calls synchronously, so they completed. The goroutines also read obj, objInfo and options after the handler has returned. I did not check whether the callers reuse those objects.

On success it calls recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...) (line 106), passing the object name where every other call passes options.Kind.
